title: JC H2 biology — cell: ultrastructure and biomolecules
subject: science

complete.problem: A micrograph shows a cell structure measuring 30 mm. Its actual length is 0.02 mm. Calculate the magnification of the micrograph.

steps.text: Recall the equation: magnification = size of image / actual size.
steps.annotation: Magnification compares the drawn or photographed size with the real size, in the same units.

steps.text: Substitute the values: magnification = 30 mm / 0.02 mm.
steps.annotation: Both lengths are already in millimetres, so no unit conversion is needed.
Magnification is a ratio, so it carries no unit.

complete.selfExplanation: Explain why both lengths must be in the same unit before dividing.

faded.problem: Calculate the surface area to volume ratio of a cube-shaped cell of side 2 micrometres.

steps.annotation: A cube has six faces, each of area side squared.
Volume of a cube is side cubed.
Divide both sides by the volume to express the ratio per unit volume.

faded.selfExplanation: The first step is shown. Say which quantity you would calculate next and how.

paired.problem: Calculate the surface area to volume ratio of a cube-shaped cell of side 4 micrometres, and state what happens to the ratio as the cell grows.
paired.solution: Surface area = 6 x 4^2 = 96 micrometres^2. Volume = 4^3 = 64 micrometres^3. Ratio = 96 : 64 = 1.5 : 1. The ratio is smaller than for the 2 micrometre cell (3 : 1): as a cell grows, its surface area to volume ratio falls, so diffusion alone can no longer supply its volume and exchange surfaces or a transport system are needed.
